items.stem:
Nidhi and Ria are very close friends. Nidhi's parents own a Maruti Alto. Ria's parents own a Toyota Liva. Both the families decide to go for a picnic to Somnath temple in Gujrat by their own cars.
Nidhi's car travels x km/h while Ria's car travels 5 km/h more than Nidhi's car. Nidhi's car took 4 hrs more than Ria's car in covering 400 km.
(i) What will be the distance covered by Ria's car in two hour?
(ii) Write the quadratic equation that describe the speed of Nidhi's car?
(iii) What is the the speed of Nidhi's car?
(iv) How much time did Ria take to travel 400 km?
(iv) How much time did Nidhi take to travel 400 km?
items.answer:
(i) Ria's car travels at (x + 5) km/h, so in two hours it covers 2(x + 5) km; once x is found to be 20, that is 2 × 25 = 50 km.
(ii) Nidhi's time for 400 km is 400/x hours and Ria's is 400/(x + 5) hours, and Nidhi takes 4 hours longer: 400/x = 400/(x + 5) + 4. Multiplying by x(x + 5), 400(x + 5) = 400x + 4x(x + 5), so 2000 = 4x² + 20x, i.e. 500 = x² + 5x, giving x² + 5x − 500 = 0.
(iii) x² + 25x − 20x − 500 = 0, x(x + 25) − 20(x + 25) = 0, (x + 25)(x − 20) = 0, so x = 20 or x = −25. A speed cannot be negative, so Nidhi's car travels at 20 km/h.
(iv) Ria's speed is 20 + 5 = 25 km/h, so she takes 400/25 = 16 hours.
(v) Nidhi takes 4 hours more, i.e. 16 + 4 = 20 hours.
items.concept: Framing an equation from a word problem
items.ocr: The book prints the label '(iv)' twice — on the fourth and fifth sub-parts; kept exactly as printed in the stem, and answered as (iv) and (v). The road photograph is decorative.

items.stem:
Optimal Pricing Strategy : The director of the National School of Drama must decide what to charge for a ticket to the comedy drama. If the price is set too low, the theatre will lose money; and if the price is too high, people won't come. From past experience she estimates that the profit P from sales (in hundreds) can be approximated by P(x) = −x² + 22x − 40 where x is the cost of a ticket and 0 ≤ x ≤ 25 hundred rupees.
(i) What is the lowest cost of a ticket that would allow the theatre to break even?
(ii) What is the highest cost that the theatre can charge to break even?
(iii) If theatre charge Rs 4 hundred for each ticket, what is the profit/loss ?
(iv) If theatre charge Rs 25 hundred for each ticket, what is the profit/loss ?
(v) What is the maximum profit which can be earned by theatre ?
items.answer:
Break even means P(x) = 0: −x² + 22x − 40 = 0, i.e. x² − 22x + 40 = 0, (x − 2)(x − 20) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 20.
(i) The lowest break-even ticket cost is Rs 2 hundred.
(ii) The highest break-even ticket cost is Rs 20 hundred.
(iii) At x = 4, P(4) = −(4)² + 22 × 4 − 40 = −16 + 88 − 40 = 32, a profit of 32 hundred.
(iv) At x = 25, P(25) = −(25)² + 22 × 25 − 40 = −625 + 550 − 40 = −115, that is a loss of 115 hundred.
(v) Completing the square, P(x) = −(x² − 22x + 121 − 81) = −(x − 11)² + 81, so the profit is greatest when x = 11 and the maximum profit is 81 hundred.
items.ocr: The book labels the substitutions wrongly — it writes 'P(2)' for the value at x = 4 and 'P(5)' for the value at x = 25 — but the arithmetic it performs is at x = 4 and x = 25 and the results 32 and −115 are right, so the labels are corrected here. Not counted as a key contradiction. Stem on page file p049, solution finishing on p050. The stage photograph is decorative.

items.stem:
Auditorium, the part of a public building where an audience sits, as distinct from the stage, the area on which the performance or other object of the audience's attention is presented. In a large theatre an auditorium includes a number of floor levels frequently designed as stalls, private boxes, dress circle, balcony or upper circle, and gallery. A sloping floor allows the seats to be arranged to give a clear view of the stage. The walls and ceiling usually contain concealed light and sound equipment and air extracts or inlets and may be highly decorated.
In an auditorium, seats are arranged in rows and columns. The number of rows are equal to the number of seats in each row. When the number of rows are doubled and the number of seats in each row is reduced by 10, the total number of seats increases by 300.
(i) If x is taken as number of row in original arrangement, write the quadratic equation that describes the situation ?
(ii) How many number of rows are there in the original arrangement?
(iii) How many number of seats are there in the auditorium in original arrangement ?
(iv) How many number of seats are there in the auditorium after re-arrangement.
(v) How many number of columns are there in the auditorium after re-arrangement?
items.answer:
(i) Originally the number of rows equals the number of seats in a row, so with x rows the total is x² seats. After the change there are 2x rows with (x − 10) seats each, giving 2x(x − 10) seats, and this is 300 more than before: 2x(x − 10) = x² + 300, so 2x² − 20x = x² + 300, i.e. x² − 20x − 300 = 0.
(ii) x² − 30x + 10x − 300 = 0, x(x − 30) + 10(x − 30) = 0, (x − 30)(x + 10) = 0, so x = 30 or x = −10. A count cannot be negative, so there are 30 rows originally.
(iii) Original number of seats = x² = 30² = 900.
(iv) After re-arrangement the seats are 900 + 300 = 1200.
(v) The rows are now 2 × 30 = 60, so the number of columns is 1200 ÷ 60 = 20.
items.concept: Framing an equation from a word problem

items.stem:
Raju and his classmates planned a picnic in zoo. The total budget for picnic was Rs 2000 but 5 students failed to attend the picnic and thus the contribution for each student was increased by Rs 20. The expanse of different item was as follows.
S. No.ArticleCost per student
1Entry ticketRs 5
2CoffeeRs 10
3FoodRs 25
4Travelling costRs 50
5Ice-creamRs 15
(i) If x is the number of students planned for picnic, find the quadratic equation that describe the situation. (ii) What is the number of students planned for picnic ? (iii) What is the number of students who attended the picnic? (iv) What is the total expanse for this picnic ? (v) How much money they spent for travelling ?
items.answer:
(i) With x students planned, each would pay 2000/x; with (x − 5) students actually going each pays 2000/(x − 5), which is Rs 20 more: 2000/x + 20 = 2000/(x − 5). Multiplying by x(x − 5), 2000(x − 5) + 20x(x − 5) = 2000x, so 20x² − 100x − 10000 = 0, and dividing by 20, x² − 5x − 500 = 0.
(ii) x² − 25x + 20x − 500 = 0, x(x − 25) + 20(x − 25) = 0, (x − 25)(x + 20) = 0, so x = 25 or x = −20. A count cannot be negative, so 25 students were planned.
(iii) Five failed to attend, so 25 − 5 = 20 students attended.
(iv) Expense per student = 5 + 10 + 25 + 50 + 15 = Rs 105, so the total expense = 105 × 20 = Rs 2100.
(v) Travelling cost = 50 × 20 = Rs 1000.
